chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Gifts are of three types: a gift of reward, a gift of conciliation, and a gift for the sake of Allah, Exalted and Majestic.'

key_terms.مُصَانَعَةٍ: Conciliation or keeping in good favor

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of gifts in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits the Prophet’s classification of gifts into three categories: reward (mukafā’a), conciliation (muṣāna’a), and devotion to Allah (lillāh). This tripartite division reflects the nuanced social ethics of early Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between transactional reciprocity, diplomatic goodwill, and pure spiritual intent. The categorization underscores the importance of intention (niyyah) in social interactions, a key theme in Shia moral theology.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The gifts are upon three aspects – A gift as a reward, and a gift for getting some work done, and a gift for (the Sake of) Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy, who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Gifts are of three kinds: One is a gift to compensate a favor, another is a gift for understanding (bribing) someone, and another gift is a gift from Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’”
